svg.title: Transaction Isolation Levels
svg.desc: Transaction Isolation Levels. What concurrent transactions can see of each other: the anomalies each isolation level allows and the defaults engines use. Step 1, Two runs at READ COMMITTED: At READ COMMITTED the report reads 51,179.03, then 47,193.60, and two sales take stock from 10 to 9. Step 2, The anomalies, named: Named: never a dirty read, but a non-repeatable read, a phantom, a lost update and write skew. Step 3, Stronger levels, retried: REPEATABLE READ keeps one snapshot and aborts B with 40001; only SERIALIZABLE stops the write skew. Step 4, Costs and other engines: Retries cost throughput and FOR UPDATE waits; MySQL's default still loses the update, with no error.

g.text: At READ COMMITTED the report reads 51,179.03, then 47,193.60, and two sales take stock from 10 to 9.
Named: never a dirty read, but a non-repeatable read, a phantom, a lost update and write skew.
REPEATABLE READ keeps one snapshot and aborts B with 40001; only SERIALIZABLE stops the write skew.
Retries cost throughput and FOR UPDATE waits; MySQL's default still loses the update, with no error.
SELECT total_thb FROM orders WHERE id = 495179
SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 42
no dirty read: B not committed
same snapshot as the first read
SELECT qty FROM stock WHERE product_id = 2892
SELECT qty FROM stock WHERE product_id = 2892
UPDATE stock SET qty = 9 WHERE product_id = 2892
two sales, but the stock fell from 10 to 9: one decrement is gone
ERROR: could not serialize access due to concurrent update
ROLLBACK · retry: reads 9 · sets qty = 8 · COMMIT
SELECT count(*) FROM shift_leads WHERE on_duty
SELECT count(*) FROM shift_leads WHERE on_duty
UPDATE shift_leads SET on_duty = false WHERE id = 1
UPDATE shift_leads SET on_duty = false WHERE id = 2
Rule: at least one lead stays on duty. Runs in step 2.
SELECT count(*) FROM shift_leads WHERE on_duty
SELECT count(*) FROM shift_leads WHERE on_duty
UPDATE shift_leads SET on_duty = false WHERE id = 1
UPDATE shift_leads SET on_duty = false WHERE id = 2
both committed: 0 leads on duty, the rule is broken · write skew
REPEATABLE READ: both commit too, 0 on duty · write skew
→ ERROR: could not serialize access due to read/write
B retries: count(*) is now 1, so Malee stays on duty
Sessions are separate psql processes; a script runs them in this exact order.
Write skew: each saw 2 on duty and changed a different row, so nothing blocked.
Retry loop: on SQLSTATE 40001, roll back and rerun the whole transaction.
Long transactions keep their snapshot longer, so they meet more 40001s.
Every transaction: BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL <the highlighted level>.
PostgreSQL never shows uncommitted data, even at READ UNCOMMITTED.
Retry deadlocks (40P01) too, and back off between attempts.
SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY DEFERRABLE: waits once, then can’t fail with 40001.
Red: the anomaly happened in our run. Green: it did not. 40001: one aborted.
Dashed: the SQL standard forbids it at that level.
MySQL: our runs on 8.4. SQL Server: from its documentation. * plain SELECTs
Retries redo work; FOR UPDATE waits; a single UPDATE locks the row briefly.
SELECT qty FROM stock WHERE product_id = 2892 FOR UPDATE
UPDATE stock SET qty = 9 WHERE product_id = 2892
UPDATE stock SET qty = 8 WHERE product_id = 2892
stock 8 after two sales, no retry
SELECT qty FROM stock WHERE product_id = 2892
SELECT qty FROM stock WHERE product_id = 2892
UPDATE stock SET qty = 9 WHERE product_id = 2892
stock 9 after two sales: a lost update, and no error at REPEATABLE READ
With FOR UPDATE: 8. At SERIALIZABLE: ERROR 1213 (40001), a deadlock.
MySQL 8.4 InnoDB · REPEATABLE READ, its default
